answer: Seat allocation picks graders from a hash-committed lottery whose randomness is only revealed after a fixed horizon of epochs, and every seat must be backed by an onyx bond escrowed for that whole horizon. So a sybil farmer cannot predict which of its identities will grade which answer at signup time, and each fresh address must lock bond capital that stays slashed if its attestations deviate from panel median. A dune of correlated accounts funded in one block therefore has to outlay horizon-long escrow on seats whose yield is a fraction of it, making the attack costlier than honest mining.
